reference.citation: Xu Zhang et al., Robust Log-Based Anomaly Detection on Unstable Log Data, ESEC/FSE 2019
reference.relevant_published_contribution: semantic log-event representations followed by an attention-based Bi-LSTM classifier for robust log anomaly detection

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The published method represents log events with semantic vectors intended to improve robustness to unstable log data.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: A trainable embedding maps integer event IDs from the frozen training-only research vocabulary to vectors. Unseen validation/test events map to the learned unknown-event row.
deviations.reason: Both detectors must consume the same leakage-controlled parser output and vocabulary so architecture, rather than an external embedding corpus, is the principal comparison.
deviations.comparability_impact: This is an architecture-style comparison, not a claim of exact reproduction of the published semantic-embedding pipeline.

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The publication evaluates log anomaly detection under its own Hadoop and service-log data construction and robustness experiments.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: The detector is trained and evaluated on labelled HDFS BlockId units with fixed 80/10/10 block-disjoint splits, a validation split, and a training-only vocabulary.
deviations.reason: The registered LogInsight-FV endpoint is block-level evidence recovery under explicit leakage controls.
deviations.comparability_impact: Published scores are contextual only; they must not be treated as directly comparable to this run’s metrics.

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The paper’s exact sequence-length and padding implementation is not copied into this study’s detector input contract.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: Sequences are truncated to a maximum length of 50 and post-padded so TensorFlow Metal/cuDNN can apply a valid right-padded mask.
deviations.reason: The HDFS experiment requires a bounded tensor shape, and right-padding is required by the selected TensorFlow backend when masking is enabled.
deviations.comparability_impact: Padding is a documented implementation choice; the parser, event order, vocabulary, prediction units, and split assignments remain fixed.

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The published architecture is an attention-based Bi-LSTM classifier, but this study does not claim the paper’s complete training environment or hyperparameter reproduction.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: Embedding dimension 128, 128 units per LSTM direction, 64 attention units, 32-unit dense layer, dropout, Adam, balanced class weights, deterministic seed reporting, validation-loss early stopping, and Keras checkpoints.
deviations.reason: These choices align the detector with the existing LogInsight research runtime and make the experiment reproducible on the shared hardware/software stack.
deviations.comparability_impact: Results identify a controlled LogRobust-style architecture check, not a reproduction leaderboard claim.

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The published detector’s original decision and reporting protocol is not used as the registered LogInsight-FV evaluation contract.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: The detector emits probabilities and provisional 0.5 metrics; the shared study pipeline will fit temperature scaling on validation predictions, select the F1 threshold on validation only, and report calibration plus detection metrics.
deviations.reason: Both architectures must be evaluated under the same no-test-tuning protocol.
deviations.comparability_impact: Final cross-detector comparisons use the shared calibration and thresholding artifacts, not raw published-paper thresholds.

deviations.published_or_reference_expectation: The published attention mechanism learns event importance for classification.
deviations.loginsight_implementation: The temporal-attention layer is retained as a model component and exposed by name, but its weights are not automatically treated as faithful explanations or shown to the LLM. Integrated Gradients remains the registered prompt-visible attribution method.
deviations.reason: The study separates predictive attention from faithfulness verification and follows the registered attribution protocol.
deviations.comparability_impact: This preserves the detector architecture while preventing an attention-plausibility assumption from changing the explanation endpoint.

known_non_deviations: The detector is supervised binary classification with a sigmoid output.
The model contains a bidirectional LSTM and temporal attention, preserving the published architectural idea.
The same parser, event ordering, prediction-unit identity, and training-only vocabulary policy are used for both study detectors.
interpretation_rule: Do not compare this run’s numerical scores directly with published LogRobust scores unless data construction, unit definition, split policy, preprocessing, and threshold protocol are demonstrably comparable.
